html:
SMTO-LLM-0058 — Provider unavailable

GUID: 1e85d0d0-80f1-5532-ba17-a2a7b493d65d
Slug: local-ai-provider-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO checked the model server program on that computer before starting it, but the program was missing, didn't respond properly, or is a kind SMTO can't start. Nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages that computer to check the model server program (vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama) is installed and opens without errors there. SMTO runs the program's help command first, and stops if the program is missing or fails.
  2. If your profile uses LM Studio or a generic OpenAI-compatible server, start that server yourself instead of asking SMTO to. SMTO can only check those servers; it can't start them.
  3. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer. The status shows whether SMTO can now start this program there.
  4. Once the status says it can, ask SMTO to start the model server again. Nothing was started this time, so trying again is safe once the program works.

What success looks like

  • The Local AI status lists the program as able to start, and the model server reaches ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Note that SMTO can't start model servers on a Windows Gateway. Don't stop programs on that computer that SMTO didn't start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway cannot manage this provider: its adapter does not advertise managed lifecycle (executable not on PATH, Windows host, or an external-only provider), or the executable's help probe failed or timed out after 15 seconds.

What this means

  • Executable help inspection failed, or the adapter did not advertise managed lifecycle support on this host. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Executable help inspection failed, or the adapter did not advertise managed lifecycle support on this host.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact executable on the selected Gateway and whether its help probe succeeds; compare platform lifecycle support.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, run the provider's help command as the Gateway's service account (vllm serve --help=all, llama-server --help or ollama serve --help) and fix any error it prints; a missing executable on the Gateway's PATH or a profile executable whose file name isn't vllm, llama-server or ollama also lands here. Managed start is unavailable on Windows Gateways; for LM Studio or generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints, manage the server outside SMTO.
  • Have the Gateway operator repair the supported executable or manage an external endpoint through its own supported controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The adapter advertises lifecycle availability and its help probe completes.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
